first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and likely helps reverse the 6% activation decline, with prior evidence of durable activation, faster time-to-value, and adoption gains. Promotional pricing is the strongest alternative given competitive pressure, but its long-term retention and revenue quality are not established, so both records should be verified before commitment.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing both current declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle: despite qualified-revenue lift, its cohort suffered 30-day retention of -12% and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Some uncertainty remains about reproducing the historical effect under current conditions.

final2.rationale: Keep the shortened-onboarding experiment. It directly addresses the completion and activation declines, and the verified record showed +13% completion, 2.1 days faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. The deeper competitor cut increases urgency but does not reverse the verified evidence that a 40% SMB discount produced -12% 30-day retention and cohorts that failed to survive first renewal. Price-related churn may require a future guarded retention-specific test, but matching prices now would conflict with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective.
